title: How to become a plugin/asset seller

posts.author: vr_scar
posts.body:
Hi all.
I have spent some time creating plugins and assets for my own game in MZ and some of which I thought would be a great for others to be able to utilize in their own creations. Some of these have taken quite a long time to develop and perfect.
I was wondering how I can become a seller on RPG MAKER with my own creations or would it be better to create my own website?
Thank in advance-
SCARRED INTERACTIVE

posts.author: Zia_
posts.body: There are a lot Plugins sold via itch.io, maybe that's the easiest way?

posts.author: AquaEcho
posts.body: Look at where other asset sellers are selling. A lot of them are on itch, Patreon, and have their own websites

posts.author: vr_scar
Timeline_man
posts.body: itch is almost certainly the easiest way that also gets a lot of traffic from indie developers, who are most likely to purchase assets.

posts.author: utunnels
posts.body: Yeah, but on the other hand, itch's search function is just bad. You probably won't get much traffic just by dropping stuff there.

posts.author: Zia_
posts.body:
utunnels said:
Yeah, but on the other hand, itch's search function is just bad. You probably won't get much traffic just by dropping stuff there.
Click to expand...
That's true, but in terms of visibility this goes for all solutions.
Getting your own website to show up on google is a challenge, and I feel like nobody would look for plugins on Patreon in the first place.
So, whatever you do, you'll have to promote your plugins additionally here in the forum for example and build up some reputation.
And, as bad as the itch search function might be - if you google for specific plugins, the relevant itch.io pages will show up.

posts.author: Undermax
posts.body:
Hey friend, let me share my experience with you:
I started in early 2024, honestly with a slightly different approach than I have now. During this time, I’ve changed a lot of things, and the question you’re asking yourself was actually one of my first big questions:
What to do about the distribution of plugins and/or resources?
The reality is that if you want people to find your content, you absolutely need to use a popular platform. You might have the best-developed resource out there, but if no one can find it, it won’t matter. (And of course, I’m not even considering factors like pricing or the type of resource you’re offering.)
So, coming back to the question about plugin distribution: the more platforms you use, the better. Get your content out there through as many channels as possible—forums, digital platforms, social media—everything helps.
It took me about eight months to finally decide to develop my own website, mainly because of my project
Undermax Cloud
(an RPG Maker MZ app designed to make all my plugins easily accessible in a visually appealing way).
In the end, I chose to make
Itch.io
my main distribution platform.
While this limits some of the customization options I’d have with my own website, it guarantees a few important things that users value:
1.
Security and transparency in transactions
​
I take user security very seriously. Sure, I could build a payment and user database system myself, but I prefer to rely on a platform that has already invested heavily in security protocols to prevent hacking or data theft.
I'm not saying Itch.io is invulnerable, but it's likely they have more experience, resources, and time to dedicate to these issues than I do. And whether we realize it or not, this is something users care about a lot.
2.
Distribution and visibility
​
Itch.io is super helpful thanks to its search system. It’s not perfect, but it's better than nothing.
When someone searches for an RPG Maker plugin, they’ll likely start with:
A search engine (Google, DuckDuckGo, etc.)
Official forums (like this site)
Popular platforms like Itch.io, Steam, or Patreon
Now, unless you’re running a major marketing campaign (paid or not), search engines probably won’t show your website in the top results for a while. Most users don’t go beyond the first 15 results before giving up or changing their search terms, so getting listed among those is crucial.
Official RPG Maker MZ forums are fantastic—they attract a lot of users and tend to rank well in search engines. But you’ll have to comply with their rules, especially regarding paid resources. I won’t go into detail here since the guidelines are clearly outlined on the site. Whether you agree with them or not, it’s important to follow the rules to avoid issues later.
Conclusion: What should you do?
​
If you're starting with free resources:
Go with the official forums—they’ll help you reach a broad audience quickly.
If you're planning to offer paid resources:
I recommend using Itch.io. Just make sure you spend time customizing your page to make it as appealing and user-friendly as possible.
And what about your website?
That depends on your goals:
Want to reach more people? Use popular platforms.
Want maximum control, customization, and freedom? Use your own website.
As I mentioned earlier—and I promise I’m wrapping up—it’s best to use as many distribution channels as you can. Just make sure you follow the rules of each platform to avoid trouble later.
I hope this helps!
Cheers!
